title: Harvesting broccoli microgreens
subtitle: When and how to cut, rinse, and store broccoli microgreen cotyledons
excerpt: Broccoli microgreens are ready to cut when the cotyledons are fully open and vivid green, around day 7 to 10 after sowing. Cut 1 cm above the medium with scissors. Broccoli cotyledons hold well in the refrigerator for up to three days after cutting.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens guides (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Standard microgreen-growing practice synthesised from extension service material.

glossaryTerms.definition: The seed leaf — the first leaf or pair of leaves produced by a germinating seed. In most microgreen crops, the cotyledons are harvested as the edible shoot. Broccoli cotyledons are oval and smooth, vivid green when fully developed. They are milder in flavour than the true leaves that follow.

The height at which microgreens are cut above the growing medium. Cutting at 1 cm above the surface leaves the root system behind and keeps compost away from the cut stems. Most brassica microgreens are cut at this height.

content.text: Broccoli microgreens are harvested at the cotyledon stage, before the true leaves appear. The harvest window is around day 7 to 10 from sowing, but the correct visual cue is more reliable than the day count: look for fully open cotyledons, vivid green throughout, 4 to 6 cm tall.

should be fully open (not cupped or folded), a vivid even green, and 4 to 6 cm tall. If the cotyledons are open but yellow-green, give another 12 to 24 hours in bright light. If tiny lobed true leaves have begun to appear from the centre, the broccoli is past peak but still usable; the flavour becomes more bitter as the true leaves develop.
Use clean sharp scissors. Work from one side of the tray to the other, cutting horizontally through the stems.

: cut 1 cm above the medium surface. This standard cut height for brassica microgreens avoids compost contamination of the stems and leaves the root system cleanly behind in the tray. The tray goes to compost after cutting; broccoli microgreens do not produce a usable second cut.

Rinse cut broccoli microgreens under cold water in a colander. Shake out excess moisture. Broccoli cotyledons are among the more robust microgreens for storage; refrigerate in a sealed container with a dry kitchen paper lining for up to three days.
For the best flavour: use within 24 hours of cutting. After 48 hours the flavour becomes slightly more bitter and the texture softens.

attrs.heading: Troubleshooting
attrs.intro: Common harvest-stage problems with broccoli microgreens.

items.symptom: Cotyledons still yellow or pale green despite being the right height
items.cause: Insufficient light during the growing phase, or blackout cover removed too early.
items.fix: Wait 12 to 24 hours in brighter light before cutting. The green colour develops when chlorophyll is produced in direct response to light.

items.symptom: Some stems have yellow seed hulls still attached to the cotyledons
items.cause: Seed hulls that didn't separate during germination cling to the cotyledon.
items.fix: Pick off attached hulls by hand before rinsing. This is normal and doesn't affect eating quality.

items.cause: Excess moisture in the storage container.
items.fix: Ensure the container has a dry kitchen paper lining to absorb excess moisture. Shake or spin the cotyledons dry before refrigerating.
